parole.testo: Inherited from Late Latin ācrus, from Latin ācer (with a change in declension), from Proto-Italic *akris, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱrós (“sharp”).

Inherited from Late Latin capus, from Latin caput, from Proto-Italic *kaput, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kauput-, *káput. Plural form capete from Latin capita. Compare the doublet șef, borrowed from French.
Inherited from Late Latin caecia, from classical Latin caecus, from Proto-Italic *kaikos (“blind”), from Proto-Indo-European *kéh₂ikos (“one-eyed”). Compare Lombard scega (“fog”), scighera (“fog”).

parole.significato: to bake (to cook in an oven)
parole.testo: Inherited from Late Latin cocere, from Latin coquere, coquō, from Proto-Italic *kʷekʷō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pekʷ- (“to cook, become ripe”).
Inherited from Late Latin coxa (“thigh”), from Proto-Italic *koksā, from Proto-Indo-European *kóḱseh₂, from *koḱs- (“joint, limb”) + *-eh₂.
Inherited from Late Latin rādīcīna, from Latin rādīx, rādīcis (“root”), from Proto-Italic *wrādīks, from *wréh₂ds. Cognate with Aromanian (a)rãdãtsinã, French racine, Sardinian radichina.

Inherited from Late Latin volēre, remodeled from Latin velle, from Proto-Italic *welō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁-.
